investigator.agent: claude-code 2.1.310 (headless claude -p, only the five MCP tools allowed)

hypotheses.hypothesis: **Payment `Charge` is the origin of the errors.**
hypotheses.predicts: sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", span_name="oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) > 0.01 unless on() sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"product-catalog|shipping|email|cart|currency|quote", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) > 0
hypotheses.evidence: At 06:42:00Z payment's Charge server spans failed at 0.032/s and none of checkout's other upstreams (product-catalog, shipping, email, cart, currency, quote) had a single failed server span, so the errors start at payment. At the baseline 06:31:23Z payment had no failed span and the query returns nothing. The agent went beyond the alerts here: alerts_at showed only ShopCheckoutErrors and ShopServiceErrors, and it found the charge span itself.

hypotheses.hypothesis: **Only part of the payment traffic failed, and the failures were brief.**
hypotheses.predicts: sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"}[5m])) > 0.05 and sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"}[5m])) < 0.9
hypotheses.evidence: At 06:42:00Z 31 % of payment's server spans failed: more than 5 % and far from all, so only part of the traffic failed. That fits a paymentFailure variant of 25 % plus noise from the low order rate (about 0.1 orders/s). Empty at the baseline 06:31:23Z, where payment had no failures. The 'brief' half is S3's.

hypotheses.predicts: sum(increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[8m])) > 0 and on() sum(increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[3m])) == 0
hypotheses.evidence: At 06:44:30Z payment had failed spans in the last 8 minutes and none in the last 3: the failed-span counter rose from 0 at the 06:37:10Z push to 8 at the 06:41:10Z push and stayed at 8 to the end of the snapshot, so the failures fit inside about four minutes (06:37 to 06:41). At the baseline 06:31:23Z the series does not exist yet and the query returns nothing.

hypotheses.why_no_query: It is a statement about the agent's own uncertainty ('don't clearly explain'), not about the shop, and the snapshot cannot settle it either way: by design no metric names a flag of the injector's pool (only cart's cartFailure and failedReadinessProbe have feature_flag series), so no PromQL query can show that a flag did or did not explain the payment errors.

hypotheses.hypothesis: That is consistent with this being a single fault, not two.
hypotheses.evidence: A single fault means payment failing while nothing else changed. At 06:42:00Z payment did fail (0.032/s), but frontend-proxy served 31.7 requests/s against about 2/s on the baseline, a traffic surge of about 15 times that has nothing to do with payment. Recommendation also went from one ListProducts call per request to about one in two (the ratio was 0.5 at 06:41Z), a third change. So the query returns nothing. The agent only looked at error series and the two alerts, and never at traffic or latency.
